chat.text: What excercise can i swap for Snatch-Grip Romanian Deadlift

Heads up: I couldn't verify against the PDF's exact printed substitution list this session — the file is too large for my reader and shell access is blocked right now. So the swaps below are matched to what this exercise is *doing* in your plan, not read verbatim off the page. I've flagged that.

**What the Snatch-Grip RDL is there to do (so any swap must match it):** a light hip-hinge for hamstrings/glutes + posterior chain, programmed deliberately easy — **2 x 8 @ ~40kg, RPE 6-7, 1-sec pause at bottom.** It is NOT meant to be a heavy grinder. Snatch (wide) grip also adds upper-back/trap work, but your chest-supported row already covers that, so the priority to preserve is the hamstring hinge.

Pick by what's driving the swap:

- **Just don't like the wide snatch grip →** **Standard-grip Barbell Romanian Deadlift.** Closest 1:1 swap. Same 2 x 8 @ 40kg, RPE 6-7, pause at bottom.
- **Grip/forearms fail before hamstrings, or want it simpler →** **Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift.** ~15-18kg per hand to start, same reps/RPE. Easy to keep light.
- **Lower back feels it / want least spinal load →** **45° Back Extension (hyperextension).** Bodyweight for 2 x 10-12, hold a plate to your chest only if too easy. Very back-friendly, hits hams + glutes + erectors.
- **Want pure hamstring stimulus, no axial load →** **Lying or Seated Leg Curl** (you already have a Seated Leg Curl anchor). 2-3 x 10-12, RPE 8.
- **Cable available, want glute/ham with minimal fatigue →** **Cable Pull-Through.** 2 x 12 @ ~25-30kg.

My default recommendation: **Standard-grip Barbell RDL** if you just want the grip gone, or the **45° Back Extension** if your lower back is the reason. Either keeps the low-fatigue intent intact.

Want me to lock one of these into Wednesday's Pull day and reprint the day? And once shell/PDF access is back I'll confirm it matches the program's own Option 1/Option 2 — tell me if you'd rather stick strictly to those.
